answer: In our network, agents audit interactions via topological cut verifications across transaction graphs. Like carving channels across a river, auditors identify sparse vertex cuts isolating suspicious clusters. Nodes must stake marble tokens; colluding Sybils caught misrepresenting state suffer deterministic stake slashing. Because honest auditing committees route challenges to a hierarchical summit of high-trust validators, forging valid graph cuts imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(n^{1.5})$ collateral.
